properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. @ajs, 2026-10-21, reading https://arxiv.org/html/2609.40169v1 (Yang, Lai, Wang, Harari, Gabrilovich, Chang, "Learning from Research: Toward Lifelong Agent Harness Evolution", Microsoft Research / UC Santa Barbara; read through a summarizer, the main text only, the appendix's failure taxonomy not read): "yes, record (1) and (2) in reflow2 as ideas".

THE PAPER: the model stays fixed and only the harness around it (tools, context, skills, memory, workflow) is changed. A candidate change is kept only if the lower end of a paired bootstrap interval of its gain on a validation task set is above zero ("H_{g+1} = H~_g if L_α(H~_g, H_g) > 0; H_g otherwise"), so a gain inside the noise is never kept. AppWorld task completion went 69.0% → 81.4% (Qwen3.5-27B).

WHY IT APPLIES: reflow2's served skills, tool descriptions and instructions ARE a harness. They change in nearly every PR, and what is checked is form (skill_lint, budgets, test_init), routing (find_tools ranks, tool_confusability 228/228, held-out paraphrases) and use (req:skill-adherence-is-measured: whether a skill was loaded). Nothing checks whether an agent does the design job BETTER after a change.

THE IDEA: a small fixed set of design tasks (drawn from the trials: a proof rung, an argument, a hub search, an adopt) run by an agent before and after a served-text change, several times each; the change's gain read with a paired interval; reflow2 0.90.0 already reads a hypothesis test as `supported` at α, and flo2-calc computes the tests, so the verdict can be a kept record.

CHEAP / EXPENSIVE: running agents on many tasks several times is the cost, in tokens and wall time. The affordable form is a small set run at release time, not per PR.

COUNTER-ARGUMENTS: (i) a fixed task set gets tuned to (that is idea (2), dec:idea-the-trials-that-find-friction-are-kept-apart-from-the-check-that-judges-the-fix); (ii) a task-completion score encodes what was measured, including what was measured wrongly (the same pushback as dec:idea-what-reflow2-can-learn-from-evaluator-guided-llm-circuit-design); (iii) by @ajs's line of 2026-10-17, running the agents is the AI arena and the harness that runs them is a test tool, while reflow2's half is recording the measurement and reading its verdict.

OPTIONS, none chosen: (a) a release-time measurement over a fixed task set; (b) per-PR, only for PRs that change served text; (c) keep today's form/routing/use checks and measure nothing more.
properties.name: OPEN — should a change to a served skill, a tool's description or the instructions be kept only when agents measurably do the job better with it, on a fixed set of tasks, with the gain's lower bound above zero?
